newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Amsterdam bourse declines comment on Fokker.
newsitem.headline: Amsterdam bourse declines comment on Fokker.

text.p: The Amsterdam Stock Exchange said on Thursday it had postponed trading in shares of bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker ahead of a statement but declined to comment on the contents or by whom it would be published.
Earlier, the Dutch Economics Ministry said it had postponed a press briefing on Fokker, planned for 1130 GMT, and said it would issue a statement later in the day.

The Dutch and Malaysian governments, Stork NV, which now owns maintenance and components unit Fokker Aviation, the Fokker administrators and Dutch industrial group Begemann have been negotiating a salvage of Fokker for weeks.
After the ministry said it would make a statement later in the day, Fokker's shares shot up by 0.55 guilders to 1.89 guilders.
Trade in shares of bankrupt companies is possible on the Amsterdam bourse but entirely at the risk of the parties involved as the bourse does not guarantee any clearing or settlement of such deals.
